devotionals.title: Serving the Lord
devotionals.scriptureText: “Serve wholeheartedly, as if you were serving the Lord, not people.” Ephesians 6:7
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Apostle Paul continues his teaching on Spirit-filled relationships by addressing how we should live out our faith in everyday places. He speaks to children, parents, servants, and masters and shows that the gospel reshapes how we relate to one another. These verses are not about hierarchy but about heart posture. He wants us to understand that every act of obedience, honor, and service becomes worship when done unto the Lord. The gospel transforms ordinary roles into sacred assignments.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. Obedience and honor reflect our relationship with God. Paul calls children to obey their parents “in the Lord”. This reminds us that obedience is ultimately an act of worship. Honor is about recognizing God’s order and responding with respect. When we honor those God has placed in our lives, we reflect the humility of Christ.

2. Leadership must be gentle and life-giving. Paul instructs fathers not to provoke their children but to raise them with nurture and instruction. Authority in the kingdom is never harsh or domineering. It is patient, guiding, and rooted in love. Godly leadership reflects the heart of the Father, firm in truth and rich in compassion.

3. Our work becomes worship when done for Christ. Paul tells servants to work with sincerity, not to impress people but to serve the Lord. And he reminds masters to treat those under their authority with justice and humility. The principle is clear: whether leading or following, we do everything as unto Christ. He is the true Master we serve.

This passage invites us to bring Christ into the ordinary rhythms of life, our homes, our responsibilities, our work. It calls us to obedience rooted in love, leadership shaped by grace, and service offered wholeheartedly to the Lord. When we live this way, even the simplest tasks become expressions of worship.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, please help me honor You in my relationships and responsibilities. Teach me to serve wholeheartedly, lead with grace, and walk in obedience that reflects Your heart.

devotionals.title: The Armor of God
devotionals.scriptureText: “Be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power.” Ephesians 6:10
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Apostle Paul reminds believers that the Christian life is not lived on neutral ground. We are in a spiritual battle1 This battle is not against people, but against unseen forces that oppose God’s purposes. Paul calls us to stand firm in the strength of the Lord. God provides everything we need, truth, righteousness, peace, faith, salvation, and His Word, to stand against the enemy’s schemes.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. Our strength comes from the Lord, not ourselves. Spiritual strength is not something we muster; it is something we draw from God’s power. We stand firm not because we are capable, but because He is faithful. The battle belongs to the Lord, and He equips us to stand.

2. God gives us armor for spiritual battles. Paul describes the armor of God; truth as a belt, righteousness as a breastplate, peace as shoes, faith as a shield, salvation as a helmet, and the Word of God as a sword. Each piece protects us from lies, accusations, fear, and temptation. This armor is a spiritual reality. When we put it on, we stand covered in Christ Himself.

3. Prayer is the posture that keeps us standing. Paul ends by urging believers to “pray in the Spirit on all occasions.” Prayer is not an accessory to the armor. It is the atmosphere in which the armor works. Prayer keeps us alert, dependent, and connected to the strength of God. It is how we fight, how we stand, and how we remain anchored in Christ.

This passage invites us to stand firm, not in our own ability, but in the power of God. We are called to put on the armor He provides. We are to pray with perseverance and to remember that victory is found only in standing in Christ.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, please strengthen me with Your power. Clothe me with Your armor and help me stand firm against every scheme of the enemy. Teach me to pray with perseverance and to trust in Your victory.

devotionals.title: Boldness for the Gospel
devotionals.scriptureText: “Pray also for me, that whenever I speak, words may be given me so that I will fearlessly make known the mystery of the gospel.” Ephesians 6:19
devotionals.body:
Apostle Paul closes his letter to the Ephesians with a request for prayer and a blessing of peace, love, faith, and grace. Even in chains, his focus is the gospel. He longs for boldness, clarity, and courage. He wants to speak fearlessly about Christ, even while imprisoned for that very message. His closing words remind us that the Christian life is sustained by prayer, strengthened by community, and anchored in the peace and grace of God.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. Boldness comes from God, not personality. Even as an apostle, preacher, and missionary, Paul still asks for prayer to speak fearlessly. Boldness is not natural confidence; it is Spirit-empowered courage. It is God giving us words, strength, and clarity when we need them most. If Paul needed prayer for boldness, so do we.

2. Ministry is strengthened through community. Paul sends Tychicus to encourage the believers and update them on his situation. Even the strongest leaders need support. The gospel is never carried alone. God uses people to strengthen our hearts, remind us of truth, and help us stand firm. Encouragement is a ministry every believer can give.

3. God’s grace sustain us. Paul ends with a blessing: peace to the brothers and sisters, love with faith, and grace to all who love Christ. Peace steadies us. Love anchors us. Faith strengthens us. Grace carries us. These gifts come from God and keep us faithful to the end.

Today’s passage invites us to pray for boldness, to value the encouragement of community, and to rest in the peace and grace God freely gives. Like Paul, we are called to make Christ known with courage, humility, and unwavering trust in God’s strength.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, please give me boldness to make the gospel known. Help me remain faithful to Christ in every season.
